minutes.headline: Personnel Committee voted to recommend new FY24 and FY25 salary grids and a higher pay grade for the pack manager.
minutes.summary: The committee finished its salary administration plan work. It chose the 1550 starting grid with a step dropped and a two and a half percent COLA for FY25, and voted on three warrant article recommendations. It set a tentative next meeting for April 30 and agreed to send the package to the select board and finance committee.

public_comment.topic: A caller said she had heard the beach director job title might change and noted a current employee holds it. The committee said it would keep the title.

votes.motion: Approve the March 11 minutes as amended (meeting dates corrected).
Recommend the FY24 grid starting at 1550 with step one dropped, and the FY25 grid with a two and a half percent COLA.
Approve the position classification warrant article, with the pack manager at grade 12, as the committee's recommendation.
Accept the salary schedule warrant article for FY24 and FY25 as read.
Change the existing sick time policy to add the new-parent sick leave language.
Recommend the same sick leave language as a warrant article to the town manager.

budget_items.what_was_said: Impact sheets were reviewed for the drop-step and COLA scenarios, with a total impact quoted for each.

budget_items.topic: Call firefighters and call EMTs budget
budget_items.what_was_said: These groups are budgeted as a group, not individually, so their cost in the impact sheet is an estimate.
FY25 includes a COLA plus a market-adjustment step. The regular step increase continues, and people at the top of the grid get a larger combined raise.
A member cited the federal government's January grid adjustment as support for asking for more than usual.
The article would transfer money from available funds to pay the FY24 and FY25 wage increases.

transfers.description: Transfer from available funds to fund the FY24 and FY25 wage increases, as worded in the warrant article

decisions.decision: Committee agreed to keep the beach director job title.
Committee agreed to recommend the pack manager move up one grade, from 11 to 12.
Members agreed all of this is a recommendation. Changes need input from the town manager and the department head.
Committee declined to reopen the Council on Aging outreach coordinator grade, which the director wanted at nine, and kept the earlier recommendation of eight.
Julie will send the package to Heather, who will forward it to both the select board and the finance committee.
A tentative next meeting was set for April 30 at 5 PM.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to recommend an FY24 pay grid starting at 1550 with step one dropped, and an FY25 grid with a cost-of-living increase.
It voted unanimously by roll call to approve the position classification warrant article, with the pack manager moved up from grade 11 to grade 12.
It voted unanimously to accept the FY24 and FY25 salary schedule warrant article, which would transfer money from available funds to pay the increases.
It voted twice, both unanimous, to add new-parent sick leave language to the sick time policy and to recommend the same language as a warrant article.
The committee declined to reopen the Council on Aging outreach coordinator grade and kept its earlier recommendation of eight; it set a tentative next meeting for April 30.

why_it_matters: The salary schedule and position classification recommendations are the basis for warrant articles that town meeting voters may be asked to approve, and the salary article would draw on available funds.
The minutes call every item a recommendation, so the select board, the finance committee, the town manager and department heads still have input before any pay change takes effect.
watch_next: The package goes to the select board and finance committee, then to the warrant articles on position grades, the salary schedule and sick leave.
A tentative Personnel Committee meeting is set for April 30 at 5 PM.
